claims.text: The scoping review identified 82 relevant studies on the application of machine learning to social determinants of health published before May 1, 2020.
More than half (56%, n = 46) of the reviewed studies on machine learning and social determinants of health used data from the United States.
Eighty percent (n = 66) of the reviewed studies utilized survey data.
Seventy percent (n = 57) of the reviewed studies employed machine learning for pure prediction tasks.
Only 10% (n = 8) of reviewed studies used machine learning for causal inference.
Only 18% (n = 15) of reviewed studies used machine learning for data curation.
Only 2% (n = 2) of reviewed studies used machine learning for algorithmic fairness.
Cross-sectional study designs were employed by 65% (n = 53) of the included studies.

evidence.description: Of the initial 8097 hits, we identified 82 relevant studies published before May 1, 2020.
More than half of the studies (n = 46, 56%) used US data.
Of the 82 studies, 80% used survey data (n = 66).
The majority of the studies employed ML for pure prediction (n = 57, 70%).
10% of studies used ML for causal inference (n = 8).
53 studies (65%) employed a cross-sectional study design.

methodologies.name: PRISMA-ScR Scoping Review Framework
methodologies.description: A systematic scoping review mapping literature on machine learning applications to social determinants of health across four electronic databases and manual searching.

limitations.text: The bibliometric search required terms to appear in title, abstract, or keywords, which may have excluded relevant studies mentioning terms only in the full text.
The review included only peer-reviewed papers, excluding conference abstracts, letters, and notes.
Many machine learning algorithms function as black boxes with low degrees of interpretability compared to traditional linear models.

future_work.text: Apply machine learning to study social determinants of health in non-US regions and utilize transfer learning to compare predictions across diverse populations.
Leverage non-conventional unstructured data formats such as text, audio, and image data for data curation in social determinants of health research.
Utilize longitudinal datasets with machine learning to evaluate the causal impact of public health interventions over time.
Expand research using machine learning for algorithmic fairness and estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects in social epidemiology.
